assumptions: This fixed public reference panel yields a provisional source-relative recommendation, not calibrated coding ability, endpoint performance or task-success probability.

The 50/50 workload weights and tier thresholds are product choices, not measured equivalences. Renormalize over available selected workloads; missing evidence is unknown, not tier C. Confidence is separate from the recommendation index.

Lower numeric priority wins. Select at most one profile/result per workload; metrics in the same source family are fallback choices, not additional votes. Break run ties by latest genuine evaluatedAt, then ascending literal cohort/evaluation/model IDs, never highest score.

Reference distributions are frozen independently of provider offerings. Changes to the provider roster or refreshed source records must not rebuild these panels. A reference distribution update requires an explicit policy-version change and renewed review.

Only the exact admitted cohort IDs and recursive recordConstraints are applicable. Unlisted task releases/configurations cannot inherit this panel and must use another accepted fallback or remain unknown.
Reference runs are deduplicated by exact raw modelId only. Preserve effort, date, precision, version and other label qualifiers; unknown checkpoint aliases are not deduplicated or inferred.

Tier C denotes the lower relative region of the selected reference panel, not absence of coding advantage or evidence of inability. Different source panels are not calibrated to a common capability scale.
Coding category is the arithmetic mean of code_generation and code_completion, requiring both published task columns. This is generation/debugging evidence, not full-repository editing.
Release identifies the task version, not evaluation time. evaluatedAt and taskCount are unknown; literal labels and reviewed identity mappings must preserve reasoning/version distinctions.

Only this single dated release is in the reference distribution; historical and newer releases are not pooled. Newer admitted releases take priority as a product freshness preference, not a score-max choice.

BigCodeBench prefill=false instruct and complete panels are omitted: 14 and 15 distinct model profiles respectively, below minimumReferenceSize=20. Llama-4-Scout's only mapped generation cohort is therefore unsupported; do not relax the gate to assign it a tier.

LiveBench 2025-05-30 and 2024 coding releases are not admitted in v1: the 2026-06-25 and 2026-01-08 panels cover all currently reviewed LiveBench model evidence. Those older cohorts remain distinct task versions, not merged reference records; newly mapped old-only evidence needs a reviewed policy update or another accepted fallback.
LiveCodeBench has no audited snapshot/importer; Arena and SWE-bench are not supported. No reference panel is inferred for them.

Only exact admitted hashed cohorts with test_cases=225, null editor_model/editor_edit_format and no architect format/flag are allowed. Accepted formats: diff, diff-fenced, whole. Missing or partial-task cohorts and architect/editor pairs are not admitted.

Polyglot requires both total_tests=225 and test_cases=225. Python requires test_cases=133 but total_tests/taskCount are unknown in admitted rows; full-suite scope is supported only by the published test_cases metadata, not an inferred known denominator.

Polyglot excludes six rows with test_cases 223/224 and three architect/editor-pair rows (one overlaps a partial-task exclusion). Python excludes 132/33/36/225-task rows; its udiff format is explicitly admitted only in the older Python family.
